page: Amazon Web Services r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2976.78. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by a weak multi-core stress-ng score of 5966.47 and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 3725.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also fall into the lower tier, with uncached large-block read and write speeds recorded at 38.45 GB/sec and 22.57 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average levels.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio but modest multi-core compute and memory bandwidth performance, the r6a.xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. Appropriate use cases include medium-sized databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth should be factored into data-transfer-heavy architectures.
